name: east-west barricade of stacked sandbags, old tyres and a rusty sheet-metal plate, tops seen from above
label: wasteland_ruins/barricade-h

answer.evidence: The metal plate has a salmon top plane (rows 4-8) with a bright edge at row 4 and a dark front-edge line at row 9. Below it is a rust-coloured vertical face (rows 10-14). The tyre stack at right has a dark ring around an open ellipse (rows 8-14, widening from 31 to 45 px) above its banded front rows 15-26. The sandbag stacks show light-grey top patches (rows 11-14) and a pale edge row at 15, then brown front faces and dark courses down to row 26. Every major part has a top surface above a front face of 3+ rows, so the whole object reads as three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small low prop, not a full building, so I compared it on shading craft only. The measured facts put it level with the references: 10 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outlines are tinted. By eye, the sandbags are layered in grey-brown with about 4 steps and per-bag highlights and shadows. The rusty plate has a lighter top edge, a mid body and a dark base, and the tyres sit in a dark tinted tone. It has fewer steps and less grain than the roof tiles and stone on the references. Even so, there is no uniform black sticker outline and no large flat fill, so a careful artist would accept it beside the references.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small low barricade, not a building with roof, walls and door, so it is a different kind from the references. On the numbers it holds up: 10 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, 0% near-flat coverage, and 0% near-neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is tinted. By eye, the sandbags, tyres and rust plate carry only about 3-4 lightness steps each, against the 5-6 steps of the reference roof tiles, which have per-tile highlights. The tyres on the right read as a nearly flat dark mass, and the sandbags are fairly smooth with little grain. The whole piece is clearly thinner and simpler than the references' scalloped roofs and speckled plaster, and it is only a few tiles in size. Because the shading is shallow and the texture is lighter than the references, I fail it when in doubt.

answer.evidence: The sheet-metal plate shows a 5-row top plane (rows 4-8) with a yellow highlight, and a dark edge line at row 9 followed by shadow before the streaked front face (rows 10-14). The sandbag courses have gray top bands (rows 11-13 and 16-18) that end in light edge lines (rows 14 and 19), with brown front faces below down to row 26. The tyre at right shows a dark oval opening, rows 9-13, set inside a widening-then-narrowing silhouette, which reads as an ellipse top. Every major part has a top surface and a front face of at least 3 rows.

styleAnswer.evidence: The references are houses and the candidate is a small barricade prop, so I judged craft rather than structure, as the assigned 'building' style kind implies. On the primary facts the candidate has 10 visible tones per tile, against 12 for h101 and 10 for h112-stone. Near-flat coverage is 0%, matching both references. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the outlines carry a tint and read as dark material tone: brown beside the sandbags and rust beside the plate. By eye, the sandbags are stacked and shaded bag by bag with about 5 steps, and the rust plate has a highlight edge and a darker underside. The tyres are the weakest part, a fairly dark mass with little internal variation, but they are not a large flat fill. The piece does not look thinner or more sticker-like than the stone reference tile, so it is acceptable beside it.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts support the candidate.
